'''Žarko Čabarkapa''' ({{lang-sr-cyrl|Жарко Чабаркапа}}, {{IPA|sh|ʒǎːrkɔ̝ tʃabǎrkapa|pron}}; born 21 May 1981) is a Serbian professional [[basketball]] executive and former player who is Vice President at BeoBasket agency.

Standing at {{height|m=2.11}}, he played in the [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] position for [[KK Beopetrol|Beopetrol]], [[KK Budućnost Podgorica|Budućnost]], [[Phoenix Suns]], and [[Golden State Warriors]]. Čabarkapa finished his playing career in 2009 due to injury.

A [[Serbia men's national basketball team|Yugoslav international]],{{refn|group=note|Čabarkapa represented then [[FR Yugoslavia]] (later [[Serbia and Montenegro]]) internationally.}} Čabarkapa won the gold medal at the [[2002 FIBA World Championship]].

==Playing career==
Čabarkapa played for a Belgrade-based team [[KK Beopetrol|Beopetrol]] and Podgorica-based team [[KK Budućnost Podgorica|Budućnost]], both of the [[YUBA League]]. When playing there, he averaged 8.6 points, 3.8 rebounds, and 1.5 assists per game.

Čabarkapa was drafted by the [[Phoenix Suns]] in the 1st round (17th overall) in the [[2003 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web |title=NBA draft 2003 |url=http://www.espn.com/nbadraft/d03/ |website=espn.com |accessdate=3 October 2019}}</ref> He moved to the [[United States]], but in his rookie season he was injured, and this limited him to only 49 games that season. In 2005, the Suns traded him to the [[Golden State Warriors]] in exchange for two second-round draft picks. With the Warriors, he played in 37 games in 2004–05, and 61 games in 2005–06. He had problems with a back injury, and his contract with the Warriors ended in 2007.

Čabarkapa's final NBA game was played on April 15, 2006, in a 86–81 win over the [[2005–06 Portland Trail Blazers season|Portland Trail Blazers]] where he recorded four rebounds in four minutes of playing time.

After leaving the NBA in 2007, Čabarkapa stopped playing competitive basketball at the age of 26, as he recuperated from injuries. In late November 2008, it was announced that he joined his old club [[KK Budućnost|Budućnost]], but only in practices, as he looked to get himself back into competitive shape. On January 16, 2009, Čabarkapa signed with Budućnost. Two days later, on January 18, he played his first competitive game in more than two years, appearing for 4 minutes in the [[Adriatic League]] clash at home versus [[KK Cibona]]. He recorded 2 points, no rebounds, and no assists.<ref>[http://www.adriaticbasket.com/stats.php?gameid=116&sez= KK Budućnost vs. KK Cibona 82:74, SC Morača, January 18, 2009.]</ref>

== National team career ==
Čabarkapa was a member of the [[Serbia men's national under-20 basketball team|FR Yugoslavia U-20 team]] at the [[2000 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]] in [[Ohrid]], Macedonia. Over eight tournament games, he averaged 8.0 points, 3.0 rebounds, and 1.6 assists per game.<ref>{{cite web |title=2000 Yugoslavia 11 - Zarko Cabarkapa |url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/25302/pid2//sid/2367/tid/390/tid2//_/2000_European_Championship_for_Young_Men_Final_Round/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191003075149/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/25302/pid2//sid/2367/tid/390/tid2//_/2000_European_Championship_for_Young_Men_Final_Round/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 3, 2019 |website=archive.fiba.com |accessdate=3 October 2019}}</ref> He was a member of the [[Serbian men's university basketball team|Yugoslavian university team]] that won the silver medal at the [[Basketball at the 1999 Summer Universiade|1999 Summer Universiade]] in [[Palma, Majorca|Palma de Mallorca]], Spain.

Čabarkapa was a member of the [[Serbia national basketball team|FR Yugoslavia national team]] that won the gold medal at the [[2002 FIBA World Championship]] in [[Indianapolis]]. Over five tournament games, he averaged 1.6 points and one rebound per game.<ref>{{cite web |title=2002 Yugoslavia 6 - Zarko Cabarkapa |url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/25302/sid/3118/tid/390/tid2//_/2002_World_Championship_for_Men/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100605083534/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/25302/sid/3118/tid/390/tid2/_/2002_World_Championship_for_Men/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 5, 2010 |website=archive.fiba.com |accessdate=3 October 2019}}</ref>

== Post-playing career ==
Čabarkapa was a sports director of the [[ABA League JTD|Adriatic Basketball Association]] from September 2015 to June 2019.

On 2 October 2019, Čabarkapa was hired as the new [[Sporting director|sports director]] for [[KK Crvena zvezda|Crvena zvezda]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Žarko Čabarkapa novi sportski direktor KK Crvena zvezda |url=https://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2019&mm=10&dd=02&nav_id=1598787 |website=b92.net |accessdate=2 October 2019}}</ref> He left the Zvezda after the end of the 2019–20 season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Fenerbahče dobija pojačanje iz Srbije |url=https://www.mozzartsport.com/kosarka/vesti/fenerbahce-dobija-pojacanje-iz-srbije/370966 |website=mozzartsport.com |accessdate=17 November 2020}}</ref>

In November 2020, Čabarkapa joined the administration staff of the Turkish club [[Fenerbahçe Basketball]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Posle Zvezde u Fener kod Kokoškova |url=https://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/vesti.php?yyyy=2020&mm=11&dd=19&nav_id=1766739 |website=b92.net |accessdate=19 November 2020}}</ref>
